opposingBeliefs: People won't work if they get free money
mainClaim: Universal Basic Income trials show recipients work similar hours while experiencing significant improvements in mental health, education, and entrepreneurship
evidence: Nikiforos, Steinbaum and Zezza (Roosevelt Institute, 2017) modeled three universal basic income designs with the Levy Institute macroeconomic model. Financed by federal debt, the largest program (a $1,000 per month payment to every adult) was projected to expand the economy by 12.56% over the baseline after eight years, after which growth returns to baseline but output stays permanently higher. Financed by household taxes, the Levy model forecasts no effect on the economy, although a version adapted to include distributional effects projects growth even in the tax-financed scenarios.
supportingPoints: Removes welfare cliff that discourages work under current systems
Reduces stress allows job searching, training, education
Enables entrepreneurship by providing safety net for risk-taking
Multiple trials across countries show consistent results
Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend (40+ years) shows no employment reduction
limitations: The cited source is a macroeconomic simulation from a policy institute, not a trial and not peer-reviewed. It says nothing about hours worked, mental health or entrepreneurship, which this argument's main claim relies on. Limited trial durations (most 1-3 years) may not reflect long-term behavior. Different results in developing vs developed nations. Funding mechanism unclear at scale. Inflation concerns if broadly implemented. Some trials had small sample sizes. Cultural factors affect outcomes.
counterCounterArguments: Funding via VAT, carbon tax, or automation tax is economically feasible
Alaska model demonstrates political viability across decades
Inflation concerns addressable through careful implementation

sourceMetadata.title: Modeling the Macroeconomic Effects of a Universal Basic Income
sourceMetadata.methodology: Macroeconomic simulation with the Levy Institute model
